title: When it feels like too much
lines: You’re okay. This feeling is strong, and it will pass.
Put your feet flat on the floor. Press down, just a little.
Look around and name five things you can see.
Now four things you can touch.
Three things you can hear.
Breathe in for four… hold for two… and out for six.
Again. In for four… and a long breath out.
You got through this moment. I’m right here.

title: Body scan
desc: Let tension go, one part at a time.
lines: Let’s settle in. Find a position that feels easy.
Let your eyes close, or rest your gaze on the floor.
Take one slow breath in… and let it go.
Notice your feet. Their weight. Nothing to change.
Move up to your legs. Let them be heavy.
Your stomach rises and falls on its own.
Let your shoulders drop, just a little.
Soften your jaw. Your forehead. The space around your eyes.
Notice your whole body, breathing.
Whenever you’re ready, come back to the room. Gently.

title: Morning reset
desc: Start the day a little steadier.
lines: Good morning. Let’s take a few minutes before the day begins.
Sit up, with your feet on the floor. Feel the ground under you.
Take a slow breath in… and let it out.
Notice how you feel right now. Tired, okay, a bit of both. All of it is fine.
Think of one small thing you’d like to do today. Just one.
Picture yourself doing it. It doesn’t have to be perfect.
One more slow breath in… and out.
You’re ready enough. Go gently today.

title: Kindness for yourself
desc: For days you’re hard on yourself.
lines: Let’s spend a few minutes being kind to you.
Put a hand on your chest, if that feels okay. Feel it rise and fall.
Think of how you’d speak to a good friend after a hard week.
Now, quietly, say those words to yourself.
May I be gentle with myself.
May I remember I’m doing my best.
May I let today be enough.
Notice any feeling that comes up. Let it be there.
Carry a little of this kindness with you.

title: Wind-down for sleep
desc: Slow breathing and a soft body scan.
lines: Let’s get ready for sleep. Lie down in a way that feels comfortable.
Breathe in slowly through your nose… and let it out through your mouth.
Again. In… and a long, slow breath out.
Let the day go. You don’t need to solve anything tonight.
Feel the bed holding you. Let it take your weight.
Soften your face. Your jaw. Your shoulders.
Let your arms feel heavy. Then your legs.
If a thought comes, that’s okay. Let it drift past like a cloud.
Stay here. Let sleep come when it’s ready.

title: Monsoon on the hills
desc: Rain on tin roofs in a quiet hill town.
lines: Tonight we’re going to a small town in the hills, in the middle of the monsoon.
There’s nothing you need to do. Just listen, and let your body get heavy.
The bus has left you at the last stop. The air smells of wet earth and woodsmoke.
You walk up a narrow lane. Rain is falling softly on the tin roofs.
At the end of the lane, a small guesthouse has a light on. Someone has left the door open for you.
Inside, it’s warm. A quilt is folded on the bed, and a cup of ginger tea waits on the table.
You sit by the window. The rain keeps its steady rhythm.
Far below, the valley is lost in cloud. The whole town is going quiet.
You pull the quilt up. It is heavy and soft. Your shoulders let go.
The rain carries on, patient and slow. You don’t have to stay awake for it.
Sleep well.

title: The night train south
desc: A sleeper berth, the rails, dark fields.
lines: Tonight you’re on the night train, heading south.
Your berth is made up with clean white sheets. A little blue lamp glows above you.
The train pulls out slowly. The station lights slide away, one by one.
Outside, the city thins into fields. Dark shapes of trees go by.
The rails keep a gentle rhythm, over and over.
Somewhere down the carriage, a chai seller calls out softly, then goes quiet.
The carriage rocks you, side to side, like being held.
A village passes, a single light in one window. Then dark fields again.
There’s nowhere you need to be until morning. The train will carry you.
Sleep well.

title: A tea garden at dusk
lines: This evening we’re walking through a tea garden, just as the sun goes down.
The rows of tea bushes curve over the hills like green waves.
The path under your feet is soft and damp. Each step is slow.
The air is cooling. The leaves smell fresh and a little sweet.
Far off, a bell rings from a small temple. Then silence.
The sky turns orange, then pink, then a deep blue.
You find a wooden bench at the top of the hill and sit down.
The garden goes still. The first stars appear.
Rest here as long as you like.
Sleep well.
